maria_pm: Hey team — quick thread on PRD updates after yesterday's degraded routing incident. Proposing three changes to the PRD + runbook. TL;DR: stricter fallback policy, explicit canary gating, and a clear SLA rollback path. Details below.

kevin_eng: +1. I'll translate into concrete acceptance criteria and flag any infra blockers.

ashley_sre: From oncall: the main trouble was ambiguity in runbook step 4 — folks hesitated about when to trigger the model fallback. Suggest adding an explicit command and a quick verification checklist.

release-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T03:12:08Z -> PROD routing-service v4.2.1 failed healthcheck on shard-7, auto-fallback engaged (logs: https://ci/internal/abc123) :warning:

jon_support: Customer impact: two customers (acme-inc, finlytics) saw generation latencies spike >10s for ~12 minutes. They asked for timeline & mitigation.

liam_cs: I'll draft comms. Need clear statement of what changed, expected recurrence risk, and steps taken.

maria_pm: Proposed changes (PRD + runbook):
- Acceptance criteria A: When route error rate (5m) for p99 token latency or error >= 5%, trigger low-latency fallback variant within 30s automatically.
- Acceptance criteria B: Canary gating: new routing policy or model variant must run on 5% traffic for >=2 hours and meet both latency and quality thresholds before full rollout.
- Acceptance criteria C: Observable guardrail: if canary fails quality similarity metric (eval set sim <95%) or p95 latency > 150ms, auto-abort; send page to SRE.
- Runbook addition: exact command examples, verification queries, and roll-forward vs rollback decision tree.

maria_pm: Example runbook snippet (for clarity):
```
1) Run fallback: /bin/rictl route fallback --policy=low-latency --shard=all
2) Verify temp routing: curl -H 'X-Test: canary' https://api.prod.redwood/v1/health | grep "fallback=active"
3) Run smoke eval (local): python tools/smoke_eval.py --suite=core_prompts --limit=50
4) If eval sim >=95% and latency p95 <150ms -> escalate to canary traffic plan.
5) If not -> rollback routing, notify customers, file incident follow-up.
```

kevin_eng: Two notes: 1) Switching variants can produce prompt drift. Add acceptance criterion: measured generation drift on core eval set <=2% compared to baseline. 2) We need a migration test in staging that simulates KV cache warmup — fallback variant will have cold cache characteristics.

ashley_sre: I'll add the exact check commands and a short verification script to the runbook. Also recommend an alert: "routing.fallback.engaged" with tags {service:routing, severity:high} that pages SRE and PMs.

jon_support: For customer comms: include the timeframe, symptom, and immediate mitigation. Liam, I'll share the logs that show request IDs to help reconciling tickets.

liam_cs: Ack. I'll prepare a one-paragraph status and a follow-up SMS template for high-priority accounts.

maria_pm: Rollout plan & owners: Maria (PRD + acceptance tests), Kevin (implementation + staging tests), Ashley (runbook + alerts), Liam (customer comms). Target ship date: 2026-04-04 EOD. If we need a faster fix, propose a hotpatch: add explicit runbook step + alert this week.

kevin_eng: Question: do we gate by model version or route policy? I'd prefer policy-based so we can fallback to a cheaper architecture without re-deploying models. That requires router support for variant labels. Is that in scope?

maria_pm: Prefer policy-based. Scope: small infra change to add variant labels + routing weight API. If it's too big, we'll fallback to model-version gate as fallback plan.

ashley_sre: Blockers: need a quick smoke test harness that can validate canary quality (<95% sim check) automatically. I can prototype this script in a day.

kevin_eng: I'll start the routing weight API RFC and the staging migration test. Posting a draft RFC link shortly.

maria_pm: OK — action items captured. I'll update the PRD with the three acceptance criteria and add the runbook snippets. Ashley: please add alert definitions to the ops repo. Kevin: RFC + staging tests. Liam/Jon: comms + log handoff.

ashley_sre: ack :white_check_mark:

kevin_eng: on it :rocket:

liam_cs: prepping comms draft now.

maria_pm: Closing note: aim to keep changes minimal and reversible. We want guardrails that are explicit, testable, and owned. If anyone hits a blocker, @maria_pm — call it out here and we'll triage.

maria_pm: (pinned)
